summary: FOPC is not a company but a small ($33M) actively managed fund-of-funds that holds 8 bond ETFs (FLXR, VGIT, IGEB, JCPB, SCHP, MBB, VTIP, PYLD), so its fair value is its NAV and it trades close to it; there is no mispricing to exploit. The real question is cost: it charges 0.87% all-in (0.60% management + 0.27% underlying fund fees) to hold ETFs you can buy directly for ~0.03-0.64%. Its 1-year total return (+1.73%) is in line with core-plus peers and ahead of AGG, but at a 52-week low as long-dated Treasury yields hit multi-decade highs. Morningstar's quantitative rating is Negative; prefer holding the underlying funds (e.g. JCPB/FLXR) directly.

valuation.method: ETF adaptation of the spec: P/E, EV/Sales and DCF do not apply to a bond fund-of-funds. Fair value = NAV (ETF creation/redemption keeps price near NAV); range set at +/-1% of last price because NAV was not available from sources read. Peer check uses 1y total return, expense ratio and yield (columns 'growth' and 'opMargin' repurposed). No analyst targets exist for this ETF.
valuation.note: On cost-adjusted basis FOPC is expensive: three of its top holdings (FLXR 25%, JCPB 15%, PYLD 5%) are available directly at 0.37-0.64% with higher yields, and the Treasury/TIPS/MBS sleeves (VGIT, SCHP, VTIP, MBB ~38%) cost a few bps. FOPC's 1y return matched peers, so the active allocation has not yet added enough to justify the fee layer.
